summary: For all k and n and every pattern tau in S_k, the number of permutations of [n] with no Hertzsprung occurrence of tau (consecutive positions, values order-isomorphic with a single shift) is at most the number with no Hertzsprung occurrence of the identity pattern of length k; the inequality is strict when k < n and tau is neither the identity nor its reverse. This is the maximal-avoidance conjecture of Bona as stated in Claesson Conjecture 3.13, including the self-overlapping patterns that the earlier argument did not cover. The proof compares first and second moments of occurrence counts.
paste_summary: Proved. For all k and n and every pattern tau of length k, the number of permutations of n elements avoiding tau in the Hertzsprung sense (consecutive positions and consecutive values) is at most the number avoiding the increasing pattern of length k, with strict inequality when k < n and tau is neither increasing nor decreasing. This settles the maximal-avoidance conjecture of Bona, stated as Conjecture 3.13 by Claesson, including self-overlapping patterns.
caveat: The 2008 Discrete Mathematics version of Bona's paper is unread (paywalled). One phrase about work associated with Claesson Conjecture 3.14 carries no citation.
title: Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture for Hertzsprung patterns
source: Anders Claesson, “From Hertzsprung's problem to pattern-rewriting systems”, arXiv:2012.15309 (2021). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.15309)
statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_k$ be the set of Hertzsprung patterns of length $k$, let $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$, and let $|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|$ denote the number of length-$n$ objects avoiding $\tau$. Write $\mathrm{id}_k$ for the identity pattern of length $k$. **Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture.** For every Hertzsprung pattern $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$ and every natural number $n$,

$$
|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|\leq |\mathcal{S}_n(\mathrm{id}_k)|.
$$

Bóna proved the inequality for non-self-overlapping patterns. The paper reports computational evidence suggesting that self-overlapping patterns also satisfy it, but gives no general proof.
